tiers.name: Hard safety
tiers.means: Kill switch, risk-gate halts, AUTO BLOCKED / live gate, MBI. These are gates, never conflicts, and are never resolvable by anyone's opinion.
tiers.example: The kill switch is engaged: every buy is blocked even if the CIO says ADD.

tiers.name: Facts
tiers.means: Identity (GUID), broker positions, pending orders and stop state, wash windows, earnings dates. A disagreement is a DATA ERROR: both values are shown, the source is fixed, and nobody picks a winner.
tiers.example: The broker shows 0 shares but the Watch row says held: ownership data error, both values shown.

tiers.name: Policy
tiers.means: Investment Policy Statement limits, read from one config key.
tiers.example: A position over its concentration limit blocks ADD until there is headroom.

tiers.name: Deterministic checks
tiers.means: Trade AI DETERMINISTIC_FAIL / BLOCKED / STALE / DATA_UNAVAILABLE and entry-state BLOCKED. They act as gates on go-actions.
tiers.example: Trade AI is STALE on QCOM: the go-action shows 'Unknown: Trade AI data' until it re-runs.

tiers.name: Judgment
tiers.means: Opinions, in this order: your recorded decision > the CIO's recorded decision > the curator stance > LLM and desk opinions (synthesis, review, defense, advisory, Hermes, analyst, Ask, rotation, signals).
tiers.example: Desk synthesis says AVOID, the CIO record says RE_ENTER: a real conflict the CIO decides with a reason.

rules.title: Freshness
rules.means: A side's age is the age of its oldest material input, not the time the job ran. A side older than its source limit is superseded (refresh it), not a conflict.
rules.example: An 8-day-old daily synthesis disagrees with today's CIO record: SUPERSEDED, the synthesis is asked to refresh.
rules.clears: The producer rewrites the compared input with fresh evidence.
rules.owner: The producer of the stale input
rules.exact_text: R1 freshness (modified): a side's age = its OLDEST MATERIAL INPUT (inputs_as_of), not its run time. Superseded when older than min(14 d, 2× its cadence): review 7 d · synthesis 14 d · curator 2 trading days · plan 7 d · quote per §7A. Refresh is queued only to a producer that writes the compared input.

rules.title: Trade AI checks gate go-actions
rules.means: Any Trade AI state other than the clear states blocks go-actions, including ADD on a held name. The label says 'Blocked: <check>' or 'Unknown: <data>'. A trade-state AVOID is an opinion (T4), not a gate.
rules.example: FATN: Trade AI BLOCKED, the CIO says ADD: the card shows 'Blocked: Trade AI check' and no buy is offered.
rules.clears: The Trade AI check passes on its next run.
rules.exact_text: R3 gates widened: any Trade AI state other than READY/WAIT/MANAGING gates go-actions, held ADD included; label "Blocked: <check>" or "Unknown: <data>"; trade-state AVOID is judgment (T4), not a gate.

rules.title: Real conflicts get a recorded decision
rules.means: A real conflict is decided by its owner and written to the decision store for that security: the sides, the decision, the reason, what clears it and when the decision expires.
rules.example: DT: CIO RE_ENTER vs desk AVOID. The CIO records 'RE_ENTER — earnings beat outweighs desk caution, expires in 30 days'.
rules.clears: The engine re-checks every side after the decision; the flag clears only when the sources agree.
rules.owner: The CIO for stance; you for protection, policy, money mismatches and flapping
rules.exact_text: R4 real conflict → owner decision in the new decision store (per GUID: sides, decision, reason, clears_when, expiry) — §17 store, operator-approved 2026-10-24 as part of the engine ledger.

coverage.gap_note: The decision writer is not activated on the live API (POST answers CONFLICT_WRITER_NOT_ACTIVATED until the operator activates it).

rules.title: Every flag says how it clears
rules.means: Every flag shows what clears it, who owns it and when the next check runs.
rules.example: 'Blocked: IPS headroom — clears when exposure falls below the limit · owner: you · next run: 16:20 ET'.
rules.clears: Not a flag itself: it is the contract every flag meets.
rules.exact_text: R5 every flag: clears_when + owner + next_run.

rules.title: Position-aware action scale
rules.means: Actions are placed on a scale that depends on whether you hold the name. Neighbouring steps agree (with a strength note); two or more steps apart, or opposite directions, is a conflict.
rules.example: Held: CIO HOLD vs desk TRIM are one step apart: agreement. CIO ADD vs desk EXIT: conflict.
rules.clears: Not a flag when the actions agree; a conflict clears when the owner decides and the sources agree.
rules.exact_text: R2→R6 position-aware ordinal scale: held ADD > HOLD > TRIM > EXIT; not held BUY/RE_ENTER > WATCH ≡ AVOID ≡ SELL. Adjacent step = agreement with a strength note; ≥ 2 steps or crossing direction (ADD vs TRIM/EXIT) = conflict.

rules.title: No CIO stance
rules.means: A name with no CIO stance shows 'No CIO stance' (HOLD if held, WATCH if not), blocks go-actions, queues a review to a working producer and shows its age.
rules.example: 24 My Watchlist rows had no stance: each shows 'No CIO stance — WATCH by default' and no buy button.
rules.clears: The CIO records a stance.
rules.exact_text: R7 missing stance (30 rows, 24 on My Watchlist): "No CIO stance" (HOLD if held, WATCH if not), blocks go-actions, review queued to a working producer, visible age.

rules.title: CIO stance too old
rules.means: CIO stance age is counted in trading days, so weekends never cause false alarms. Past the first limit, positive actions wait; past the second, the stance needs a refresh.
rules.example: The CIO stance on QCOM is 3 trading days old: ADD waits for a fresh review; HOLD still shows.
rules.clears: The CIO refreshes the stance from fresh evidence.
rules.exact_text: R7b stance staleness in TRADING hours: > 2 trading days gates positives; > 10 → needs refresh (no weekend false alarms).

rules.title: One shared vocabulary
rules.means: Every source's label is mapped through one shared vocabulary. A label nobody mapped is shown as a data error, never guessed.
rules.example: A desk writes 'ADD_ON_PULLBACK': DATA ERROR 'Unmapped stance', the source must use the shared vocabulary.
rules.clears: The source uses a mapped label.
rules.exact_text: R8 vocabulary: one shared map (also used by cio_prospect_builder.posture); unmapped labels (ADD_ON_PULLBACK, RESEARCH_MORE, MORE_RESEARCH, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, "HOLD / MONITOR", BUY_READY, NO_ACTION, DEFER, SELL_TAXABLE) = visible DATA_ERROR.

rules.title: Stances per symbol, gates per account; wash windows everywhere
rules.means: Opinions are about the symbol; gates are about an account. A wash window from any taxable loss sale blocks buys in every account, because an IRA buy permanently disallows the loss.
rules.example: You sold SCHG at a loss in the taxable account: a buy in the Roth IRA is blocked until the wash window ends.
rules.clears: The wash window ends.
rules.exact_text: R9 stances per symbol, gates per account; a wash window from any taxable LOSS sale gates buys in ALL accounts (an IRA buy permanently disallows the loss); ONE wash-sale implementation (4 disagree today).

coverage.gap_note: The engine rule is implemented. Matrix prerequisite 4 (one wash-sale implementation across the site) is tracked separately; this page does not verify it.

rules.title: Options are not equity stances
rules.means: An option outcome is never read as a stance on the stock. The engine only cross-checks the two when they contradict each other.
rules.example: You hold a long call while the equity stance is EXIT: that contradiction goes to you.
rules.clears: The owners record the cross-instrument decision.
rules.exact_text: R10 instrument scope: option outcomes are never equity stances; cross-instrument check only on contradictions (long call vs EXIT).

rules.title: Three or more sides
rules.means: When three or more sources disagree, there is one flag listing every side. The display defaults by precedence, a recorded decision is required, and there is no majority vote.
rules.example: SCHG: CIO HOLD, desk TRIM, advisory ADD: one flag with all three sides; the CIO decides.
rules.clears: The owner records one decision with a reason and the sources agree.
rules.owner: The CIO (you when an operator or CIO side is in the split)
rules.exact_text: R11 N-way splits: one flag listing all sides; display default by precedence; recorded decision required; no majority vote.

rules.title: Broker position first
rules.means: A pending fill freezes evaluation for that name. If a stance disagrees with a fill, that is an ownership data error.
rules.example: A stop is awaiting fill on SPCX: no stance is judged until positions and the fill reconcile.
rules.clears: Positions and the pending fill reconcile.
rules.exact_text: R12 broker/position fact first: a pending fill freezes evaluation for that name; stance-vs-fill mismatch = ownership DATA_ERROR.

rules.title: Concentration headroom
rules.means: ADD waits for headroom under the Investment Policy Statement limit for that kind of holding. Diversified funds have their own fund-level limit (operator decision 2026-10-24). Missing fund holdings are a gap, never assumed to be zero.
rules.example: A single stock above its limit: ADD needs your decision. A broad fund near its limit shows a near-limit warning.
rules.clears: Exposure falls below the limit, or you decide.
rules.exact_text: R13 ADD gated by IPS headroom (12% single name; one key; today 12/15/8 disagree); diversified funds (SCHD) get a fund-level rule — operator decision needed. [Operator decision 2026-10-24: broad diversified funds are not held to the single-name cap; limits live in config/investment_policy_statement.json as the one source.]

rules.title: Failed model output is not an opinion
rules.means: A failed or partial model answer is not an opinion: it is never a side and never clears a flag.
rules.example: The watch-review worker errors on a model id: its empty answer is ignored, the old flag stays.
rules.clears: Not a flag: the failed output is simply excluded.
rules.exact_text: R14 failed/partial model output = no opinion; never a side; never clears a flag.

rules.title: Hysteresis (no flip-flopping)
rules.means: A decision holds until a side changes its action or its conviction moves by the set number of points. A new flag needs the set number of consecutive runs before it shows.
rules.example: Conviction wobbles 69 → 71 → 70 over three runs: one flag, not three.
rules.clears: A side changes action or conviction moves past the threshold.
rules.exact_text: R15 hysteresis: a resolution holds until a side changes ACTION or conviction moves ±5; a new flag needs 2 consecutive runs.

rules.title: Unresolved identity blocks everything
rules.means: If the security's identity is unresolved, every action is blocked. Sources are joined by GUID only, never by ticker text.
rules.example: GLAS identity is UNRESOLVED: no action is offered until the GUID is confirmed.
rules.clears: The identity owner confirms the GUID.
rules.exact_text: R16 unresolved identity gates every action (GLAS actionable while UNRESOLVED today); sides join by GUID only.

rules.title: Expired and unwatched rows
rules.means: A name you no longer watch, or a row that expired, never flags. It is archived, not deleted.
rules.example: You removed AXTI from My Watchlist: its old disagreement no longer shows anywhere.
rules.clears: Not a flag.
rules.exact_text: Expired/unwatched rows never flag (archived, not deleted).

rules.title: Timestamps
rules.means: A time without a timezone, or one that cannot be read, is a data error. A missing time counts as stale, never as fresh.
rules.example: A desk row stamped '2026-10-24 09:30' with no zone: DATA ERROR, the producer must stamp a real time.
rules.clears: The source corrects its evidence timestamp.
rules.exact_text: Naive/unparseable timestamps = DATA_ERROR; missing time = stale.

rules.title: Agent escalations
rules.means: When agents disagree inside one synthesis, that lowers the synthesis's confidence. It is not a disagreement between sources.
rules.example: TSLA '6 agent conflicts' inside a synthesis: shown as low confidence, not as six conflict flags.
rules.clears: Not a flag.
rules.exact_text: Agent escalations (TSLA "6 agent conflicts") are intra-synthesis confidence, not a cross-source conflict.

rules.title: Paper trades and your decisions
rules.means: Paper signals and paper positions are never sides. Your decisions carry a reason and an expiry, and never override hard safety (T0) or facts (T1).
rules.example: You record ADD on a name while the kill switch is on: the decision is kept, the kill switch still blocks.
rules.clears: Not a flag.
rules.exact_text: Paper signals/positions are never sides. Operator decisions carry reason + expiry and never override T0/T1.

code.match: T4 operator > recorded CIO > curator > opinions

never_auto.label: Hard safety gates (T0): kill switch, risk-gate halts, live gate
Stop and protection state on a held name
Money figures that disagree between pages
Job schedule disagreements (registry vs crontab vs n8n)
The same conflict reopening again and again
Three-way or wider splits that include you or the CIO
A held name with SELL/EXIT on one side and ADD on the other

never_auto_matrix_text: T0 gates · identity mismatches · ownership/position disagreements · stop-state or pending-fill mismatches · held name with SELL/EXIT vs ADD · policy breach vs ADD · wash windows · cross-instrument contradictions · ≥3-way splits including an operator/CIO side.

text.held: You hold it: ADD > HOLD > TRIM > EXIT.
text.not_held: You don't hold it: a buy family action, or stay out (WATCH, AVOID and SELL all mean stay out).
text.rule: Neighbouring steps agree (strength note). Two or more steps apart, or opposite directions (ADD vs TRIM/EXIT), is a conflict.

concentration.midrange_note: Funds with 30–49 holdings are treated as Narrow or thematic fund unless you class them.

states.means: The engine found a real conflict, gate, data error or operator item.
states.who: Conflict engine opens it; the owner is named on the flag

states.means: A review was queued to the owner (the CIO for stances).
The owner recorded a decision with a reason and an expiry.
states.who: The CIO, or you for protection, policy, money and flapping items

states.means: On its next run the engine re-checked every side and the sources agree.
Newer evidence replaced one side; nothing to decide.
A side changed again after it cleared or was decided.
states.who: Conflict engine; repeated reopening goes to you

lifecycle.cadence_design: Designed cadence (DESIGN.md §8): n8n lane conflict-resolver every 15 minutes in market hours, plus 16:20 ET and 07:30 ET; dry-run, then 2 trading days of shadow, then live.
